sentences.span: Goldman's own trading desk also notes ... global equities weakened "as investors continued to de-risk from AI-capex and AI-financing exposure."
sentences.why: The 11% AI-chip loan piece documents lenders demanding sharply higher yields to finance the AI buildout and explicitly ties equity weakness to AI-financing de-risking; the JPM afternoon briefing (20406) shows ASML fell 3.9% 'despite a beat-and-raise,' supporting the 'beating its own sales targets does not change that' clause.

sentences.span: the company upgraded its 2026 revenues to €44-45bn (vs €43-45bn prior)... The message from ASML is we cannot meet the demand we have from customers.
sentences.why: 2026 sales guide raised and demand-exceeds-capacity message both confirmed; the 3.9% fall is confirmed verbatim in 20406 ('ASML (-3.9% despite a beat-and-raise)').

sentences.span: if 11% is what it takes to clear a GPU loan in a market that, according to Goldman's Privorotsky, is still being bought on dips, it's worth asking what it costs after the next bad headline
sentences.why: The BTIG 'sell any bounce in SOXX after seven straight losses' half is fully supported (20376, Krinsky: 'SOXX ETF down 7 days in a row... lean into on the sell side'). But the only source tying Privorotsky to dip-buying is about appetite for GPU-backed private credit/loans, not semiconductor/hardware equities; recasting it as 'the hardware dip ultimately gets bought' changes the subject from a credit-market observation to a bullish equity call and frames it as a direct bank-vs-bank counter to BTIG's stock call, which the source does not support.

sentences.span: The strength in core inflation was broad-based, with accelerations in shelter and core goods inflation... The Fed can, and should, look through one-time supply shocks. What it can't do is look through a demand shock
sentences.why: Second straight core upside surprise confirmed in 20388/20277; shelter/goods as the drivers and PNC's framing that demand-driven components (vs. a gasoline-type supply shock) are what the Fed can't wave off support the editorial framing.

sentences.span: core CPI rose 0.34% m/m (0.29% in August)... core CPI rose 2.6% (from 2.4%)
sentences.why: Matches 0.3% vs 0.2% expected (per PNC 20268: 'increasing 0.33% against an expectation of 0.2%') and the 2.6% from 2.4% annual move exactly.

sentences.span: OER increasing by 0.35% month-over-month... concentrated in the Midwest (+0.68%, SA by GS)
sentences.why: Goldman source confirms OER (homeowners' housing cost) +0.35% and Midwest +0.68% exactly; PNC (20268) confirms diesel costs replacing tariffs as primary goods-inflation driver verbatim.

sentences.span: Over the past three months, core CPI inflation has increased at a 3.4% annualized pace.
sentences.why: Exact match, correctly attributed to PNC.

sentences.span: we estimate that the core PCE price index rose 0.32% in September (vs. our expectation of 0.20% before the CPI release)... The upward revision to our September core PCE forecast
sentences.why: Goldman explicitly raised its core PCE estimate on the CPI data; core PCE is standard shorthand for the Fed's preferred inflation gauge.

sentences.span: The market moved to price October as roughly a coin flip, which feels appropriate... We continue to believe the Fed will hike in December and again in March
sentences.why: Coin-flip framing for October matches PNC verbatim; multiple desks (PNC, TS Lombard's 90% Dec-hike pricing in 20259, Goldman's 87% Dec odds in 20332/20328) converge on December being far less contested than October.

sentences.span: October rate hike odds jumped to just over 50% on the news... I wouldn't rule out another hike on October 28th [odds] shot up from about 5bps to about half of a 25bps rate hike
sentences.why: PNC (~50%) and Scotiabank (20240, odds up to roughly half a hike, i.e. ~50%) both register near-50% odds right after the print and both frame the hike as still live, satisfying 'two desks say the print keeps it alive.'

sentences.span: Several members have indicated that they want to see more data before hiking again, which has raised the bar for another increase already at the 28 October meeting.
sentences.why: Verbatim match, correctly attributed to SEB.

sentences.span: market now pricing in hike probabilities of 35% for October, and 87% in December
sentences.why: Exact match, Goldman source, describes the pricing at/near the close.

sentences.span: Raised our December 2026 Brent price forecast to $90/bbl (from $85/bbl) given ongoing downside risks to oil supply.
sentences.why: Exact match, Goldman source; Brent last ~$106 confirmed in 20365 ('Brent Oil @ 106.26'); 106-90=16 checks out.

sentences.span: Brent oil in 3m: scenario-weighted implied vs latest market price (USD/b): Implied: 97.0 Current: 100.6
sentences.why: Exact match of the $97 scenario-weighted figure against the $100.6 market price cited in SEB's own note.

sentences.span: 123 S&P names are up 25% or more -- while only 42 are down 25% or more... Net exposure on Goldman's global prime book is in the 10th percentile of the past year
sentences.why: Exact match on both figures, correctly attributed to Pasquariello/Goldman.
